description.p: A privacy-first desktop browser. Ad and tracker blocking is compiled into the engine, so a blocked request never leaves the machine and the browser needs no per-request callback that could become a browsing log.

Credentials and notes live in an encrypted vault that is never sent anywhere. This Flatpak stores everything inside its own sandbox and requests no access to your home directory; file choices go through the desktop portal, so the browser is handed the one file you picked.

Fingerprint Divergence. The canvas, audio, and graphics readouts sites use to recognize your browser get small site-specific noise: each site sees a different reading, and the readings change again when the browser restarts. On by default, with a switch in the Privacy panel that applies to new tabs.
Release notes now travel inside the signed update manifest, so the update panel can tell you what an update contains before you install it.
Hovering a link now shows where it goes, in a small readout at the bottom left. Deceptive characters that could make a link read as a different site are stripped before anything is shown.

Camera, microphone, location and notification requests are refused until you allow them, and an allowed site has to ask again next time you start the browser. Changing a permission reloads the page, with a warning first so you can save your work.
Pages loaded over plain HTTP can no longer reach devices on your own network.
Copying a link without tracking parameters now also unwraps known redirect wrappers, so the address you copy is where the link actually goes.
The browser warns when its phishing blocklist sources go stale.

Copying a link from the right-click menu works again. On Linux the whole right-click menu works again: opening a link in a new tab, the private and quarantine tabs, and the navigation entries were all doing nothing.
Panels no longer show the page through them on Windows.
The vault now shows Premium Time Left where you cannot miss it, and this build can verify a Premium token for the first time.
Wording fixes throughout.
The photo check now finds text that is too faint to see, like white on white, and shows you what it says. The colour measurement is a Rust port of XLiteOCR, EdgeXene's open-source OCR engine.
The right-click menu works on Windows. It never opened: the engine only raises its context-menu event while default menus are enabled, so a menu built with them disabled was never asked for.
A Theme panel, with nine accent colours and a choice of dark, white or black browser chrome.
Updates can download in the background once verified. Installing still waits for you, every time.
Updates can arrive as a small patch instead of a whole browser, when one is published for the version you run.
Update traffic goes through the private tunnel when one is imported, and fails rather than going around it.
Global Privacy Control is sent, tracking parameters are stripped from addresses, and more trackers are blocked.
Private Tunnel: import a WireGuard configuration and send only this browser's traffic through it. Fails closed, never falls back to a direct connection.
The tunnel row in Tab Activity is measured, not assumed, and says when a change needs a restart.
Banners are no longer clipped when a panel closes; Integrity and Updates are reachable from Ctrl+K.
The interface copy was rewritten in plain language throughout.
The vault locks when the workstation locks or sleeps.
Right-click opens links in a quarantine tab; save pages as PDF with a provenance record.
The malicious-host list has its own signing key and refreshes hourly.
List hygiene: URL-shaped feed junk rejected, bare platform suffixes tripwired.
Unreleased test-build version, burned: operator test builds carried this number. Its features ship in 0.9.55.
Site information and per-site cookie clearing from the address bar.
Ctrl+K opens a command palette for every toolbar action.
A diagnostic report you can copy or save, with no browsing history in it.
A first-run walkthrough of the controls that are not self-explanatory.
An opt-in Beta update channel.
Saved passwords can be offered and filled, matched on exact site.
Ephemeral tabs report the engine's answer, not the request.
A page can no longer close the browser by failing to open a tab.
Updates panel states the automatic check schedule in full.
Not published through the update channel.
First release served over the signed update channel.
Page zoom, a malicious-host blocklist, and encrypted-DNS choice.
Initial packaged build.
Final mark and wordmark.
